the viscosity of poly (vinyl alcohol)/silica hybrid nanocomposite solutions was higher than the viscosity of poly(vinyl alcohol) solutions.

the solution rheology of polymer/sillica hybrid nanocomposites prepared by the sol-gel method using tetraethoxsilane (TEOS), which was carried out at a pH range of 0.5 to 2.0.

the rheological properties of polymer/silicahybrid nanocomposites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the solution rheology of PVA/sillica nanocomposites is more complicated than that of either ACM/silica or ENR/silica nanocomposites, and the results obtained are dependent on the concentration of P VA and TEOS, and the pH of the solution.
PVA/silicacomposites exhibited Newtonian behaviour and the solution viscosity was found to increase with increasing silica content.

the solution viscosity of the PVA30 hybrid nanocomposite was greater than the viscosity of PVA, and that the solution behaviour of the PVA/TEOS hybrid nanocomposite could be described by a modified Guth-Smallwood model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PVA/sililca hybrid nanocomposites exhibit pseudoplastic behaviour when the concentration of silica is increased to 30 wt% or more, but the nanocomposites exhibit Newtonian behaviour when 5 or 7-5 wt% of silica was incorporated.
the PVA/sol-gel nanocomposites are Newtonian and pseudoplastic depending on the concentration of the components and the concentration of TEOS.
the solution rheology of PVA/sililica hybrid nancomposites is more complicated than that of the other two systems, ACM/silica and ENR/silica.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the solution rheology of polymer/sillica hybrid nanocomposites is dependent on the polymer matrix and the silica content.
the rheological behavior of polymer/sol-gel hybrid nanocomposites is strongly dependent on the nature of the polymer and the silica concentration.

the PVA/siO 2 hybrid nanocomposites exhibited a greater rise in viscosity than either the ACM or ENR nanocomposites, and that they obeyed a different relationship for the variation in viscosity with silica loading.
